terms.title: Glucocorticoid receptor (GR)
terms.definition: A ligand-activated transcription regulator encoded by NR3C1 that mediates glucocorticoid signaling.
terms.application: A steroid enters a cell, binds its intracellular receptor, and changes transcription of responsive genes.
terms.caution: GR activation is context-dependent; observing GR target genes does not prove a specific drug exposure.

terms.title: Pembrolizumab
terms.definition: A therapeutic monoclonal antibody that binds PD-1 and blocks an inhibitory immune checkpoint.
terms.application: An antibody prevents PD-1 signaling on T cells to support antitumor immunity in some cancers.
terms.caution: It targets PD-1, not PD-L1 directly; benefit is tumor- and context-dependent.

reference.label: Topalian et al., NEJM (2012), PD-1 mechanism

terms.title: Dexamethasone
terms.definition: A potent synthetic glucocorticoid used, among other indications, to manage vasogenic edema around brain tumors.
terms.application: A patient with tumor-associated brain edema receives a steroid that changes inflammatory signaling.
terms.caution: Reducing edema is not equivalent to treating malignant cells; it can confound immune transcriptomes.

reference.label: The management of brain edema in brain tumors (2004)

terms.title: Mural cells
terms.definition: Vessel-associated support cells, primarily pericytes and vascular smooth-muscle cells.
terms.application: Cells surrounding vascular endothelium help stabilize a small vessel.
terms.caution: Mural cells are not synonymous with endothelial cells.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Tumor stroma
terms.definition: Nonmalignant supporting elements of a tumor, including extracellular matrix and context-dependent stromal or vascular cells.
terms.application: A tumor section contains extracellular matrix, vascular support cells, and fibroblastic populations.
terms.caution: Stroma composition varies by tissue; it does not include malignant cells by definition.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Myeloid cells
terms.definition: A broad immune-cell grouping including monocytes, macrophages, granulocytes and some dendritic cells.
terms.application: A brain tumor contains macrophage-like immune populations and infiltrating monocytes.
terms.caution: Microglia are distinct resident CNS macrophages but are often grouped with myeloid populations analytically.

terms.title: Fibroblasts
terms.definition: Stromal cells that produce and remodel extracellular matrix components.
terms.application: A connective-tissue cell deposits collagen and modifies surrounding matrix.
terms.caution: Marker expression can overlap with other stromal cells; context is needed for annotation.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Endothelial cells
terms.definition: Cells lining the inner surfaces of blood and lymphatic vessels.
terms.application: Cells form the vascular barrier between circulating blood and tissue.
terms.caution: Endothelium is distinct from pericytes and smooth-muscle mural cells.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Single-cell multiome
terms.definition: Joint measurement of multiple molecular modalities from the same cell or nucleus, often RNA expression plus chromatin accessibility.
terms.application: One nucleus yields both its transcriptome and ATAC accessibility profile.
terms.caution: Paired single-cell multiome does not automatically preserve spatial location.

terms.title: Proliferative state
terms.definition: A cellular state with active cell-cycle, DNA-replication, or mitotic transcriptional programs.
terms.application: A malignant cluster has high MKI67 and other S/G2M-associated transcripts.
terms.caution: A proliferative program can overlap with other malignant cell-state identities.

terms.title: AC–gliosis–hypoxia continuum
terms.definition: A study-specific continuum of astrocytic-like, glial injury-response and hypoxia-associated malignant expression states.
terms.application: A GBM atlas orders astrocytic-like programs toward gliosis and hypoxic transcription.
terms.caution: This is a particular GBM atlas interpretation, not a universal class or proven trajectory for every cell.

terms.title: NPC–neuronal-like state
terms.definition: A GBM malignant-cell program resembling neural progenitor and neuronal differentiation features.
terms.application: A malignant subgroup shows developmental neuronal markers such as DCX or STMN2.
terms.caution: Transcriptional resemblance does not mean the malignant cell became a normal neuron.

terms.title: NPC–OPC-like state
terms.definition: A GBM malignant program resembling neural progenitors and oligodendrocyte precursor cells.
terms.application: A malignant cluster expresses an OPC-associated program including OLIG genes or PDGFRA.
terms.caution: This state name is study-specific and does not independently establish a normal cell lineage.

terms.title: Oligodendrocytes
terms.definition: Central nervous system glial cells that produce and maintain myelin around axons.
terms.application: A mature CNS glial cell wraps axons in myelin to support efficient signal conduction.
terms.caution: Oligodendrocytes are different from OPCs, which are progenitor cells.

terms.title: Lymphocytes
terms.definition: Immune cells including T cells, B cells and natural killer cells.
terms.application: A tissue immune compartment contains CD3-positive T cells and other lymphoid populations.
terms.caution: Natural killer cells are lymphocytes but are not T cells.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Clonal organization
terms.definition: The spatial or hierarchical arrangement of genetically related cell populations within a tumor.
terms.application: Somatic variants distinguish subclones that intermingle across tumor sections.
terms.caution: A transcriptional state is not necessarily a genetic clone.

terms.title: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS)
terms.definition: Sequencing of genomic DNA across the genome to detect genetic variation and structural changes.
terms.application: Researchers profile tumor DNA broadly to characterize SNVs and copy-number alterations.
terms.caution: WGS measures DNA, not RNA expression, and coverage or assay design limit what can be detected.

terms.title: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
terms.definition: Detection and visualization of proteins in tissue using antibodies and a labeling system.
terms.application: Antibody staining identifies protein localization in preserved histological sections.
terms.caution: Protein staining is not a direct measurement of the corresponding RNA.

terms.title: Intratumor heterogeneity
terms.definition: Genetic, transcriptional, phenotypic or spatial variation within a single tumor.
terms.application: Two biopsies from one GBM show different mixtures of malignant states.
terms.caution: Intratumor variability is distinct from variation between patients.

terms.title: Biopsy
terms.definition: Removal of cells or tissue from a living patient for diagnostic or research examination.
terms.application: A surgeon samples part of a brain lesion for histopathology.
terms.caution: A localized biopsy may not represent the full spatially heterogeneous tumor.

terms.title: IDH-wild-type
terms.definition: A molecular designation indicating no qualifying IDH1/IDH2 mutation is detected under the relevant classification and testing criteria.
terms.application: A diffuse glioma is classified after evaluating its IDH mutation status.
terms.caution: A negative screen for only IDH1 R132H may not exclude rarer IDH1/2 mutations in all cases.

terms.title: Spatial niche
terms.definition: A localized tissue neighborhood with characteristic cellular composition and molecular context.
terms.application: A vessel-adjacent tumor neighborhood combines mural cells, endothelial cells and nearby malignant cells.
terms.caution: Spatial co-occurrence alone does not prove functional cell-cell signaling.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Tumor microenvironment (TME)
terms.definition: Nonmalignant cells, matrix, vasculature and extracellular signals that interact with tumor cells.
terms.application: Immune, vascular and stromal cells occupy the environment surrounding malignant cells.
terms.caution: TME varies across tumor regions and cannot be reduced to immune cells alone.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Patient-derived xenograft (PDX)
terms.definition: A model in which tumor tissue or cells from a patient are implanted into a host animal, usually immunodeficient.
terms.application: Human tumor cells are transplanted into a mouse to study growth and treatment response.
terms.caution: Host microenvironment and immune context can differ substantially from the patient's tumor.

terms.title: Neural progenitor cells
terms.definition: Immature neural-lineage cells capable of proliferation and differentiation into neural cell types, depending on context.
terms.application: A developmental cell generates downstream neuronal or glial descendants.
terms.caution: Progenitor potential varies by region and developmental stage; it is not identical to pluripotency.

terms.title: Malignant cells
terms.definition: Neoplastic cells with cancer-associated features such as invasive growth and genetic or regulatory abnormalities.
terms.application: Single-cell tumor profiling separates cancer cells from normal immune and vascular cells.
terms.caution: A single marker rarely establishes malignancy; genetic and tissue context are important.

terms.title: Injury-response states
terms.definition: Transcriptional states enriched for programs also activated by tissue stress, inflammation or wound responses.
terms.application: Malignant cells express wound-associated or reactive-glia-like genes.
terms.caution: Expression resemblance to an injury response does not prove an injury happened to each cell.

terms.title: Mesenchymal-like (MES-like)
terms.definition: A tumor transcriptional phenotype with mesenchymal-associated and often inflammatory or injury-response genes.
terms.application: A GBM malignant population expresses CD44, VIM or CHI3L1-associated programs.
terms.caution: MES-like does not mean conversion into fibroblasts or necessarily canonical epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.

terms.title: Cellular postal-code problem
terms.definition: A conceptual analogy for how molecular guidance cues direct cells to particular tissue destinations.
terms.application: A migrating cell interprets receptor-ligand cues to reach its tissue target.
terms.caution: This is a conceptual research problem, not a defined experimental assay.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Spatially resolved transcriptomics
terms.definition: RNA measurement technologies that retain location information within tissue.
terms.application: A tumor section yields expression values along with spatial coordinates.
terms.caution: Some technologies profile multi-cellular spots rather than individual cells.

terms.title: In situ hybridization (ISH)
terms.definition: Localization of specific DNA or RNA sequences in preserved cells or tissues using complementary probes.
terms.application: A labeled RNA probe reveals where a target transcript is located in a tissue section.
terms.caution: Probe hybridization detects nucleic acid, not protein.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Cellular interactions
terms.definition: Direct or indirect influences between cells, through contact, soluble factors or other mechanisms.
terms.application: A ligand-expressing cell may influence receptor-bearing neighbors.
terms.caution: Co-expression and spatial proximity support hypotheses but do not themselves prove signaling.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Spatial expression patterns
terms.definition: Variations in RNA or protein abundance across locations in a tissue.
terms.application: One gene is enriched near the necrotic margin, another around vessels.
terms.caution: A patterned map can reflect changing cell composition rather than regulation within a cell type.

terms.title: Tissue composition
terms.definition: The identities and abundances of cell populations and structural constituents in a tissue sample.
terms.application: An analyst estimates the relative fractions of immune, vascular and malignant cells.
terms.caution: Composition estimates depend on measurement resolution and annotation quality.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Microenvironment
terms.definition: The immediate cellular, molecular and extracellular surroundings of a cell or tissue region.
terms.application: A macrophage experiences neighboring cells, soluble factors and matrix stiffness.
terms.caution: Microenvironment is a broader concept than tumor microenvironment.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Reverse transcription
terms.definition: Synthesis of complementary DNA (cDNA) from an RNA template using reverse transcriptase.
terms.application: An RNA-seq library workflow converts RNA to cDNA before amplification.
terms.caution: This is RNA-to-DNA; conventional transcription is DNA-to-RNA.

reference.label: Stark et al., Nat Rev Genet (2019)

terms.title: Spliceosome
terms.definition: The dynamic RNA-protein machinery that removes introns from many eukaryotic pre-mRNA transcripts.
terms.application: snRNP-containing machinery recognizes splice sites and joins flanking exons.
terms.caution: Not every intron in biology uses the major spliceosome.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: Spatial proteomics
terms.definition: Methods measuring protein abundance or location with spatial context preserved.
terms.application: Multiplexed antibody imaging maps tissue protein signals across cells.
terms.caution: Measured proteins and detectable targets depend on the assay panel.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Multimodal spatial data
terms.definition: Spatially anchored measurements from two or more modalities, such as RNA, proteins or histology.
terms.application: A tissue region has matched expression, cell morphology and antibody-staining features.
terms.caution: Different modalities may come from adjacent sections rather than exactly the same cells.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Gene expression imputation
terms.definition: Computational estimation of missing or unmeasured expression values from available data and assumptions.
terms.application: A model predicts genes absent from a spatial panel using a reference atlas.
terms.caution: Predicted RNA is not experimentally measured ground truth.

terms.title: In situ
terms.definition: Latin for 'in the original place'; in biology, measurements or processes examined within their native spatial context.
terms.application: Investigators detect RNA directly in preserved tissue rather than after dissociation.
terms.caution: 'In situ' describes location or context; it is not one specific assay.

reference.label: Gulati et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol (2025)

terms.title: Heterogeneity
terms.definition: Variation among cells, tissue regions or samples in measured characteristics.
terms.application: Different regions or cells differ in expression or morphology.
terms.caution: Always specify the level of variation: within tumor, between patients or across cells.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Bulk RNA sequencing
terms.definition: RNA sequencing of a pooled cell population, yielding aggregate expression per sample.
terms.application: A tissue lysate produces one expression profile combining immune and tumor cells.
terms.caution: Bulk data do not directly identify which cell expressed a transcript.

reference.label: Stark et al., Nat Rev Genet (2019)

terms.title: Nucleotide
terms.definition: A nitrogenous base linked to a pentose sugar and one or more phosphate groups.
terms.application: DNA and RNA polymers are assembled from nucleotide building blocks.
terms.caution: A nucleoside lacks the phosphate group present in a nucleotide.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: MGMT
terms.definition: O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase, a repair protein removing alkyl lesions from O6-guanine.
terms.application: Some alkylating-agent-induced DNA damage is repaired by a direct-reversal enzyme.
terms.caution: MGMT promoter methylation is a biomarker; it is not identical to measuring protein activity.

terms.title: Tumor infiltration
terms.definition: The invasion and spread of tumor cells into adjacent nonmalignant tissue.
terms.application: Malignant glioma cells extend away from the dense tumor core into surrounding brain.
terms.caution: Infiltration is not equivalent to metastatic dissemination to another organ.

terms.title: Necrosis
terms.definition: Cell or tissue death accompanied by loss of membrane integrity and structural breakdown.
terms.application: A tumor histology section contains a region of dead tissue.
terms.caution: Necrosis is not equivalent to apoptosis, and its morphology requires interpretation.

terms.title: Cellular debris
terms.definition: Remnants of damaged, dying or dead cells, including fragments of membranes and organelles.
terms.application: Histological regions contain fragments of cells after tissue damage.
terms.caution: Debris is not a distinct viable cell type.

terms.title: Neurons
terms.definition: Excitable nervous-system cells specialized for information processing through electrical and chemical signaling.
terms.application: A cortical cell propagates action potentials and releases neurotransmitters at synapses.
terms.caution: Not every neuron fires classic action potentials in the same manner.

reference.label: Gulati et al., single-cell & spatial review (2025)

terms.title: Identity covariance matrix
terms.definition: A covariance matrix equal to the identity: each component has variance one and distinct components have zero covariance.
terms.application: A multivariate distribution uses Σ = I as its covariance structure.
terms.caution: Zero covariance does not generally imply independence except under additional assumptions such as joint Gaussianity.

terms.title: Multivariate standard normal distribution
terms.definition: A multivariate Gaussian distribution with zero mean vector and identity covariance matrix.
terms.application: A d-dimensional random vector follows N(0, I_d).
terms.caution: Its components are independent standard normals because the joint distribution is Gaussian.

terms.title: DNA methylation
terms.definition: Covalent addition of a methyl group to DNA bases, commonly cytosine at CpG sites in mammals.
terms.application: CpG methylation patterns are profiled to study gene regulation and tumor biology.
terms.caution: Methylation does not uniformly silence every gene; effects depend on genomic context.

reference.label: Smith et al., Nat Rev Genet (2025)

terms.title: Copy-number variation (CNV)
terms.definition: A genomic DNA segment present in different copy numbers relative to a comparison genome or cellular baseline.
terms.application: One tumor clone gains a chromosomal segment, another loses a segment.
terms.caution: RNA-based CNV inference is indirect and should not be treated as DNA ground truth.

terms.title: Introns
terms.definition: Sequences transcribed into precursor RNA and usually removed during splicing.
terms.application: The spliceosome excises an intervening region between exons.
terms.caution: Introns may have regulatory functions; not all transcripts are spliced in the same way.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: Exons
terms.definition: Transcribed regions retained in a mature RNA product after splicing.
terms.application: Two coding segments are joined after an intervening intron is removed.
terms.caution: Exons may include untranslated regions; exon does not mean protein-coding.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: Spliced RNA
terms.definition: RNA molecules in which designated intronic regions have been removed through splicing.
terms.application: Sequencing detects reads spanning exon-exon junctions.
terms.caution: Spliced RNA is not necessarily older, translated or exported from the nucleus.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: Macrophage-rich regions
terms.definition: Tissue areas with an elevated relative abundance of macrophages.
terms.application: A histology or spatial RNA map shows a concentrated myeloid macrophage compartment.
terms.caution: Marker-based regional enrichment may mix macrophages and other myeloid populations.

terms.title: Hypoxia / hypoxic
terms.definition: A biological state or environment with reduced oxygen availability.
terms.application: A poorly oxygenated tissue zone activates oxygen-response transcriptional programs.
terms.caution: Hypoxia-associated gene expression is not itself a direct oxygen measurement.

terms.title: Ribonucleotides
terms.definition: RNA building blocks containing ribose, a nitrogenous base and phosphate group(s).
terms.application: A polymerase extends an RNA strand using ribonucleotide triphosphates.
terms.caution: RNA uses uracil rather than thymine as a canonical base; ribose differs from deoxyribose.

reference.label: Stark et al., Nat Rev Genet (2019)

terms.title: Single-stranded nucleic acid
terms.definition: A nucleic acid with one polynucleotide strand rather than a paired duplex.
terms.application: Many RNA molecules are single-stranded but fold into local base-paired structures.
terms.caution: Single-stranded does not imply absence of intramolecular base pairing.

reference.label: Wilkinson et al., Annu Rev Biochem (2020)

terms.title: Histopathology
terms.definition: Microscopic examination of tissue architecture and cellular morphology for disease characterization.
terms.application: A pathologist examines H&E-stained tumor tissue for cellular atypia and necrosis.
terms.caution: Histopathological appearance and molecular diagnosis may provide complementary information.
